ai.description: *Hebius lacrima* is a small snake with a dark brown body and a distinctive black subocular streak resembling a teardrop. It features a pale nuchal collar and keeled dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Hebius lacrima* is best distinguished by the distinctive, teardrop-shaped black subocular mark beneath its eye, which is absent in other similar Indian keelbacks.
ai.habitat: *Hebius lacrima* inhabits dense evergreen forests in the northeastern Indian subcontinent, typically found near streams at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Crying Keelback is primarily nocturnal and possesses a distinct defensive behavior: it secretes a foul-smelling fluid from nuchal glands when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hebius lacrima* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Crying Keelback (*Hebius lacrima*) is endemic to the northeastern Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya, occurring at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
